cues: Opens by stating an interpretation of the ambiguous request ("I've read 'order the build' as...") and closes with an offer to adjust if the user meant something else
Every phase ends with an explicit "Gate" pass/fail criterion, which suggests a structured verification step
The riskiest piece (CRDT convergence) is deliberately put first, and the plan states this rationale more than once
It includes a dependency diagram, a parallelization note, a risk/mitigation table and a bottom-line summary, which looks like a prescribed template
Some phases (8, 10) have no gate and the plan has typical generic-LLM features such as team sizing and week estimates, which pulls the estimate toward the unstructured baseline
